key_insight: Agent collaboration admits linear convergence guarantees when local proposals account for cross-agent effects and pass a global objective check, with an error floor that vanishes under exact corrections.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a principled way to coordinate parallel AI agents while checking that merged updates improve a shared solution.
method: Model the shared solution as blocks, with each agent optimizing one block using a cross-block correction.
Globally check proposals and merge noninterfering updates.
Allow interfering updates after checking their combination; convergence rates reflect how well proposals combine.
evidence_signal: GPT-OSS-120B routing experiments report collision-free plans in every three-agent run, roughly 2× faster median search with six agents on a larger task, and about 30% less team search time using the best checked proposal combination; SQLite query planning and synthetic tasks were also tested.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on correction accuracy and the cost of globally evaluating individual proposals and their combinations.
paper_title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
